climate.overview_html: The Copernicus C3S July 2026 bulletin confirms a new all-time global ocean surface temperature record of 21.00°C — surpassing the previous mark of 20.92°C from 2023 — with marine heatwaves simultaneously blanketing the Atlantic and Mediterranean coastlines. New Copernicus analysis reveals that Europe's parched soils amplified June–July surface temperatures through a self-reinforcing drought–heat feedback loop, pushing the Rhine to its lowest level since 1880 and the Danube to an all-time record low in Budapest. China released its 15th five-year climate plan (2026–2030) targeting a 17% carbon intensity cut, while today's Carbon Brief China briefing flags a new coal five-year plan that conspicuously avoids setting a peak-coal year. The BAMS 2025 State of the Climate documents oceans at record warmth for the third consecutive year and the Greenland Ice Sheet shedding 129 gigatons of ice in 2025.

items.headline: Copernicus: July 2026 Sets All-Time Record Global Ocean Surface Temperature at 21.00°C — Marine Heatwaves Blanket Atlantic and Mediterranean
items.summary: July 2026 mean global sea surface temperature (60°S–60°N) hit 21.00°C, surpassing the prior July 2023 record of 20.92°C. Record or near-record marine heatwave conditions persisted along the entire Atlantic seaboard and western Mediterranean coast throughout the month. The European summer heatwave was materially amplified by the anomalously warm sea surface. El Niño conditions in the equatorial Pacific contributed additional warmth on top of long-term anthropogenic ocean heat accumulation.

items.headline: Parched Ground Amplified Europe's Record June–July Heat: Copernicus Quantifies Soil–Moisture Feedback at Continental Scale
items.summary: Copernicus satellite data confirm that drought-desiccated soils across western and central Europe radiated heat upward rather than releasing moisture through evapotranspiration, amplifying surface air temperatures during Europe's record June–July heat episodes. The self-reinforcing loop — dry soil drives faster warming, which accelerates further soil drying — operated at quantified, measurable scale across the continent and helps explain why 2026's heat anomalies have exceeded model projections. The Rhine reached its lowest level since records began in 1880; the Danube set a Budapest all-time low.

items.headline: China's 15th Five-Year Climate Plan (2026–2030): 17% Carbon Intensity Cut, Carbon Market Expansion, No Major New Ambition
items.summary: China's Ministry of Ecology and Environment — co-signed by 18 departments — released the 15th five-year plan for climate change. The headline target is a 17% reduction in carbon intensity, but the plan also changes the methodology for measuring carbon intensity, making direct comparison with prior targets difficult. Carbon Brief's Q&A analysis finds no major new emission targets; the plan consolidates existing policies and signals continued clean-energy buildout and carbon market expansion, but introduces no acceleration of the 2060 neutrality timeline or new 2030 NDC commitments.

items.headline: State of the Climate in 2025: Oceans at Record Warmth for Third Consecutive Year; Greenland Sheds 129 Gigatons of Ice
items.summary: The 2025 State of the Climate report (American Meteorological Society, NOAA-led, 625 authors in BAMS Vol. 107 No. 8) documents oceans at record temperatures for a third consecutive year. All major climate indicators — CO₂, CH₄, sea level, ocean heat — set new records for the second year in a row. Greenland Ice Sheet lost approximately 129 gigatons of ice. Some Arctic permafrost zones and boreal forests shifted from net carbon sinks to net sources. Average European temperatures have risen ~2°C since the 1960s; extreme high temperatures in parts of Europe have spiked up to 10°C above historical baselines.

items.headline: China's 15th Coal Five-Year Plan Avoids Setting a Peak Year; BRICS Bloc Condemns EU CBAM as 'Discriminatory'
items.summary: China's 15th five-year plan for the coal industry (2026–2030) aims to peak consumption 'during this five-year period' without specifying a year — a deliberate ambiguity. A companion oil and gas action plan 'markedly elevates' gas as an indispensable stabilizer for hard-to-electrify industries. Xi Jinping statements reaffirmed China's 2030 NDC and 2060 neutrality commitments. The BRICS bloc joint statement condemned the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) as a 'unilateral, punitive, discriminatory' measure inconsistent with international law.

major_events.name: Typhoon Saudel (17W) — Post-Marianas, Targeting Okinawa Then Korea/Japan
major_events.status: TS → CAT 4 IMMINENT · TRACK SHIFTING NORTH
major_events.impact: After close passes within 6 nm of Agrihan and 26 nm of Pagan (Northern Marianas), Saudel is rapidly intensifying in record-warm western Pacific SSTs with near-zero wind shear. JTWC forecasts Category 4 by Sunday; Okinawa approach (~500 km SE) expected by Tuesday. Extended-range ensemble models diverge widely on a final track: Korea landfall (KMA guidance), Kyushu/Shikoku (JMA), or eastern China — all remain in the cone. Super-typhoon potential present on higher-resolution ensemble members.

major_events.name: Invest 92L — Atlantic Tropical Disturbance
major_events.impact: NHC-monitored system west of the Cape Verde Islands carrying up to 80% 7-day development probability, tracking westward toward the Lesser Antilles. Could organize into a tropical depression or named storm before reaching the eastern Caribbean this weekend, bringing heavy rainfall to the USVI and Puerto Rico.

major_events.name: US South Heat Dome — Texas to Carolinas
major_events.impact: Heat indices of 110–115°F persist across the Gulf South through today. Dozens of daily temperature records broken during the multi-week stretch; some all-time August records threatened in Georgia, South Carolina, and the Florida Panhandle.

major_events.name: Midwest Severe Storms and Flash Flooding
major_events.impact: Stalled frontal boundary and Gulf moisture maintaining multi-day flooding and severe storm threat across Plains and Midwest. Prior derecho delivered 99 mph gusts in Indiana; Level 2/5 severe risk corridor persists.

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Lala — Post-Hawaii Recovery
major_events.impact: Lala has spun out to sea well west of the Hawaiian Islands; visitor operations largely restored. Recovery ongoing in the Kaʻū district (Big Island): Māmalahoa Highway (Route 11) remains closed; partial water-service outages continue. 100+ structures damaged or destroyed.

weather.overview_html: Typhoon Saudel has cleared its close passage past Agrihan and Pagan in the Northern Marianas and is now rapidly intensifying over record-warm western Pacific waters — JTWC forecasts Category 4 by Sunday and an Okinawa approach by Tuesday, with the final track to Korea, eastern China, or Japan's main islands still highly uncertain among ensemble models. In the Atlantic, Invest 92L now carries a 70–80% development chance as it moves toward the Lesser Antilles, a sign the Atlantic main development region is finally awakening in what has otherwise been a quiet 2026 season. Tropical Storm Lala has spun out to sea west of Hawaii, with recovery ongoing in the Kaʻū district — roads closed, water-service repairs underway — following 100+ structure losses on the Big Island. The US Southern heat dome continues to post 110–115°F heat indices across the Gulf South through August 21.

items.source: Korea JoongAng Daily / JTWC / Zoom Earth
items.headline: Typhoon Saudel Rapid Intensification Post-Marianas — Cat 4 Forecast Sunday, Okinawa Approach Tuesday; Korea/Japan Track Uncertain
items.summary: As of August 21 (03:00 UTC), Saudel was ~348 km east of Saipan, tracking north-northwest at 22 km/h with maximum wind speeds of 20 m/s. JTWC forecasts rapid intensification to Category 4 in record-warm SSTs and sub-5-kt wind shear, with an Okinawa approach (~500 km SE) by Tuesday. Beyond that, extended-range guidance diverges sharply: KMA guidance carries the storm toward Korea, JMA toward Kyushu/Shikoku, and some ECMWF ensemble members toward eastern China. Super-typhoon intensity remains in play on higher-resolution ensemble members.

items.headline: NHC Designates Invest 92L With 80% TC Development Probability as Atlantic Main Development Region Activates
items.summary: Invest 92L, a loose convective cluster west of the Cape Verde Islands, has been assigned up to 80% probability of tropical cyclone formation within 48 hours and 7 days by NHC. Tracking westward toward the Lesser Antilles, the system could organize into a tropical depression or named storm before reaching the eastern Caribbean this weekend — bringing heavy rainfall and gusty winds to the USVI and Puerto Rico. NOAA's 2026 Atlantic hurricane season outlook remains below-normal, though the main development region is increasingly primed.

items.headline: Lala Spins Out to Sea; Big Island's Kaʻū District Remains Closed as Hawaii Recovers From 100+ Structure Losses
items.summary: Tropical Storm Lala has moved well west of the Hawaiian Islands and poses no further threat to the chain. Visitor operations have largely resumed at most Big Island destinations. Māmalahoa Highway (Route 11) between South Point Road and Pāhala remains closed to through traffic; partial water-service outages persist in Naʻālehu and Waiōhinu as repair crews address damaged service lines. Over 100 structures were damaged or destroyed during Lala's passage, with the Kaʻū district sustaining the heaviest losses.

items.headline: US South Heat Dome Reaches Day 21 — 110–115°F Heat Indices Persist Across Gulf South Through August 21
items.summary: The persistent heat dome over the US South continues to deliver dangerous heat index values of 110–115°F from the Texas coast through Memphis, coastal Georgia and South Carolina, and the Florida Panhandle on August 21. Dozens of daily maximum temperature records have been broken during the multi-week event; several stations are approaching all-time August temperature records. Elevated mortality risk for outdoor workers, elderly populations, and those without air conditioning. A gradual pattern change is not expected until late next week.

renewables.overview_html: The largest deal of the cycle: Brookfield Renewable agreed to acquire Aypa Power from Blackstone for a ~$3B equity / $7B enterprise value — the largest battery storage acquisition in North American history — doubling Brookfield's operating battery capacity to 6 GW and expanding the combined pipeline to 80+ GW (detailed in Industry News). Against that institutional capital tailwind, a federal judge granted the Trump administration's request to remand construction permits for EDF's 2.8 GW Atlantic Shores offshore wind project — the latest federal setback for US offshore wind. Meanwhile, US wind and solar generated 20% of total national electricity in H1 2026, up 10% year-on-year and outpacing both coal and nuclear despite the policy headwinds.

items.headline: US Wind and Solar Reach 20% of Electricity in H1 2026 — 10% Output Growth Despite Expiring Federal Incentives
items.summary: Wind and solar jointly generated 20% of US electricity in the first half of 2026, outpacing both coal and nuclear for the period — a first. EIA data shows combined output grew 10% year-over-year despite the expiration of some IRA-era federal incentives, driven primarily by utility-scale solar additions commissioned in late 2025. Growth has continued even as interconnection backlogs, transformer shortages, and policy uncertainty slow new project starts.

items.headline: Trump Administration Wins Court Remand of EDF Atlantic Shores 2.8 GW Offshore Wind Construction Permit
items.summary: A US federal court judge granted the Trump administration's Bureau of Ocean Energy Management request to reconsider construction permits for EDF's Atlantic Shores offshore wind project — up to 2.8 GW off the New Jersey coast. The ruling introduces significant timeline uncertainty for one of the few remaining large-scale US offshore projects still in active permitting. The decision follows a series of administrative actions over the past 18 months that have stalled or cancelled multiple projects across the Northeast.

science.overview_html: Google DeepMind published WeatherNext Cyclones in Nature and simultaneously open-sourced three model variants under Apache 2.0 — the first DeepMind weather model weights released for commercial use. The system delivers an additional 24 hours of tropical cyclone warning lead time, outperforms ECMWF ENS on 96% of TC targets, and was validated operationally by the National Hurricane Center during Hurricane Melissa in the 2025 season. Combined with ECMWF's AIFS-TC (arXiv:2608.09959, previously covered), TC intensity and track forecasting has advanced by roughly a decade of historical progress in a single year of AI-model development. Also newly presented at ACM KDD 2026, UniExtreme — the first weather foundation model built for 18 compound extreme event types — finds that approximately 86% of US weather timesteps in 2024 involved composite extremes, underscoring why single-hazard models systematically underperform on tail events.

items.headline: WeatherNext Cyclones Published in Nature and Open-Sourced — AI Delivers +24h TC Warning Lead Time, Validated by NHC on Hurricane Melissa
items.summary: Google DeepMind's WeatherNext Cyclones achieves state-of-the-art tropical cyclone track, intensity, and wind structure forecasting, now published in Nature. Outperforms ECMWF ENS on 96% of TC targets; 3-day forecasts match the accuracy historically achieved only at 2-day leads — a net one-day improvement in actionable warning time. Uses Functional Generative Networks producing 1,000 ensemble members at 28 km resolution (111 km for the mini variant). Three variants open-sourced on GitHub under Apache 2.0: WeatherNext Cyclones, WeatherNext 2, and WeatherNext 2-mini (Colab-runnable). NHC used it during Hurricane Melissa's rapid intensification and Jamaica landfall in 2025. First DeepMind weather model weights released for commercial use.

items.headline: UniExtreme: First Foundation Model Designed for 18 Compound Extreme Weather Types — 86% of 2024 US Timesteps Were Composite Extremes
items.summary: UniExtreme is the first weather foundation model trained jointly on labeled data from 18 real-world extreme event types (heatwaves, heavy rain, severe cold, compound events) together with general meteorological reanalysis. An Adaptive Frequency Modulation (AFM) module captures region-wise spectral signatures of extreme atmospheric states via learnable Beta-distribution filters; an Event Prior Augmentation (EPA) module conditions on regional extreme patterns. Analysis reveals that approximately 86% of US weather timesteps in 2024 involved composite extremes — multiple co-occurring hazards — highlighting why single-hazard models systematically miss the most damaging events. Presented at the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining.

items.title: WindBorne Systems Raises $37M Series B to Expand AI Weather Balloon Network and WeatherMesh Forecasting Models
items.body_html: WindBorne Systems closed a $37 million Series B co-led by Khosla Ventures and Galvanize, with Translink Capital, Biprogy, and Lux Capital participating — bringing total funding past $62 million at a reported $250 million valuation. The company operates the world's largest long-duration autonomous weather balloon fleet (600+ simultaneously airborne units) and feeds the data into its proprietary WeatherMesh forecasting models. WeatherMesh-6 currently ranks as the most accurate publicly benchmarked weather forecasting model. WindBorne tripled both annual revenue and balloon count over the past year. Proceeds will expand the constellation, increase computing resources, and fund next-generation WeatherMesh model development.

items.title: MSCI Completes $120M Acquisition of First Street — Property-Level Physical Climate Risk for 2 Billion+ Structures Goes Into MSCI Platform
items.body_html: MSCI completed its acquisition of First Street on August 3, 2026, for $120 million upfront plus potential revenue-based earn-out payments. First Street's physics-based multi-hazard models translate climate risk — flood, wildfire, extreme heat, wind — into financial impact estimates at the individual property level for more than 2 billion structures worldwide. Results are now reported in MSCI's Sustainability and Climate segment. The deal was announced in June and closed ahead of schedule; it positions MSCI's climate analytics directly against Moody's RMS, CoreLogic, and Verisk in the fast-growing property-level physical risk intelligence market, where demand is accelerating from mortgage lenders, insurers, and institutional real-asset investors.

items.title: H1 2026 Climate Tech VC Report: $26.1B Raised (+55% YoY) — Data Centers Displace Energy as the Largest Funding Vertical
items.body_html: Total climate tech venture capital reached $26.1 billion in H1 2026, up 55% year-on-year and the strongest first half since 2022, per the CTVC H1 2026 Climate Tech Investment & Innovation Report. Built Environment / low-carbon data centers accounted for 34% of all funding (vs. 3% a year prior), growing more than 800% year-on-year — driven by DayOne's $4.5B Series C (largest climate tech deal since 2020) and Nscale's $2B round. Deal count fell 25% as capital concentrated in fewer, larger bets tied to the AI "speed-to-power race." Climate adaptation tech grew 64% to $5.5B in 2025; ICEYE's $521M satellite raise was the largest climate resilience deal outside energy and transport, reflecting the shift from modeled risk to lived-reality demand.

items.title: Brookfield Renewable to Acquire Aypa Power from Blackstone — Largest Battery Storage Deal in North American History at ~$7B Enterprise Value
items.body_html: Brookfield Renewable agreed to acquire Aypa Power — North America's largest standalone battery energy storage developer and operator — from Blackstone Energy Transition Partners at approximately $7 billion enterprise value ($3 billion equity). Aypa brings 3 GW of operating and under-construction assets plus a 20+ GW development pipeline across the US and Canada. The acquisition doubles Brookfield's operating battery capacity to ~6 GW and expands its combined development pipeline to more than 80 GW. A shareholder vote is expected in October 2026; close targeted by year-end. At $7B enterprise value, the deal surpasses all prior North American battery storage transactions and signals institutional conviction that large-scale storage — not natural gas — is the answer to the AI data-center power demand surge.
